conf.description: aws-vpcflow flow / parquet-s3: maps the already-typed Parquet columns (INT_32/INT_64) to ECS - protocol/tcp-flags/traffic-path decode, epoch-seconds timestamps to event.start/event.end/_time. Scope is deliberately limited to the 10 integer-typed columns this work order tables; every other selected column (srcaddr, dstaddr, action, log-status, vpc-id, etc.) is STRING-typed identically to the text feed and maps to ECS exactly as that feed does, per the work order's own notes - not duplicated here.

conf.comment: aws-vpcflow / flow / parquet-s3. Cribl's S3 Parquet reader has already decoded row groups to typed, named fields - no _raw line to split, unlike the text feed. tcp-flags/traffic-path are HYPHENATED source names (THE BIG ONE trap), read via __e['tcp-flags']/__e['traffic-path'] bracket access, never path syntax. traffic-path's 8-value decode uses AWS's own published table (docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-log-records.html, fetched live - not guessed); the previous quarantined attempt at this field had an unbalanced ternary, so this version casts Number() once into a flat scratch field first rather than repeating it 8x. network.transport covers only tcp/udp/icmp/icmpv6 - the full IANA table was not supplied and is not invented. Direct route, no guard hop.

functions.description: record dataset, format, the hyphenated-source-name handling, and the traffic-path/protocol scope decisions

step 1: cast the two hyphenated-source integer columns into FLAT clean-named scratch fields (no dots), read via bracket access. Deliberately flat, not the final aws.vpcflow.* nested target yet - eval.add with a dotted name builds real nested structure, and reading that back via __e['a.b.c'] (a single flat bracket key) would silently miss it, the same flat-vs-nested landmine the brief warns about for dotted SOURCE keys, self-inflicted here if skipped

step 2 of the derived-field computation, from ORIGINAL vendor names (protocol/start/end/version) and the step-1 scratch fields, before the batched rename: bounded protocol resolution, tcp-flags bit decompose (fin=1/syn=2/rst=4/ack=16, no arrow/filter per constraint 3), the 8-way traffic-path decode against AWS's published table, and epoch-seconds-to-ms/duration/_time (never @timestamp, constraint 1)
batch-rename the five clean 1:1 typed columns to their ECS targets

tag event.dataset (no hyphen, constraint 5) and event.provider; drop the clean-named originals consumed into event.start/end/_time/version above, and the hyphenated tcp-flags/traffic-path originals via glob (the literal hyphenated names are rejected by eval.remove)
